say: Same dress. Higher price. More sales.
Why? Your brain reads prices from left to right, and it's lazy.
It sees the nine first, and stops.
So nine ninety-nine feels like nine. Not ten.
Psychologists call it, the left-digit effect.
show: Psychologists call it the left-digit effect.

say: That's why almost nothing costs a round number.
Four ninety-nine. Nineteen ninety-nine. Ninety-nine ninety-nine.
The fix? Round every price up in your head.
So next time a price ends in nine, remember why
